description:
As a penetration tester, you want to automate a simple vulnerability scanning routine using shell scripting. Please create a shell script at /home/user/scan_targets.sh that does the following: 1. Reads a target list of IPs or hostnames from a text file located at /home/user/targets.txt. Each line in this file contains a single target (there will be three entries: 192.168.0.10, 192.168.0.20, and test-host.local). 2. For each target, performs a basic port scan for ports 22 (SSH), 80 (HTTP), and 443 (HTTPS) using nc (netcat) with a timeout of 1 second per port. 3. Outputs the results to a log file at /home/user/scan_log.txt. The log file should list each target and its port status in the following exact format: 
Target: <target>
Port 22: <open/closed>
Port 80: <open/closed>
Port 443: <open/closed>
For example: 
Target: 192.168.0.10
Port 22: open
Port 80: closed
Port 443: closed

Target: 192.168.0.20
Port 22: closed
Port 80: open
Port 443: open

Target: test-host.local
Port 22: closed
Port 80: closed
Port 443: closed
Ensure your script is executable. You do not need to install additional packages; assume that nc is already available. Once the script is finished running, the scan_log.txt should exactly match the output format above with no additional text or blank lines beyond those shown. Please do NOT use sudo in your script.
truth:
Before the task begins, the following file exists:
- /home/user/targets.txt with these exact contents:
  192.168.0.10
  192.168.0.20
  test-host.local

Agent must create the following files:
- /home/user/scan_targets.sh (must be executable, i.e. chmod +x)
- /home/user/scan_log.txt (results file with the following contents):

Target: 192.168.0.10
Port 22: open
Port 80: closed
Port 443: closed

Target: 192.168.0.20
Port 22: closed
Port 80: open
Port 443: open

Target: test-host.local
Port 22: closed
Port 80: closed
Port 443: closed

No extra lines, no trailing or leading whitespace in the output log, and no additional console output is required. The agent must use netcat (nc) with -z and -w 1 to perform the scan, looping for each target and port as outlined.
